issues.description: Regex may miss unitless zero time values (e.g., `transition-duration: 0`)
issues.detail: The fast-path regex `/\dm?s/i` requires the literal `s` or `ms` unit after a digit. CSS permits unitless `0` as a valid time value (e.g., `transition-duration: 0`). If the existing rule previously flagged such declarations as below the minimum, this short-circuit will silently skip them and introduce a behavioral regression. The author should confirm with a test that unitless-zero declarations are either still flagged or were never flagged before.

issues.description: Regex can match digit+s/ms inside strings, urls, or identifiers, weakening the fast path
issues.detail: Values like `url("icon1s.png")` or `content: "5ms"` would pass the `HAS_TIME` test and fall through to the slower valueParser path even though no real time token exists. This is a correctness-safe false positive (no semantic change) but slightly limits the performance win the PR is aimed at. Not a blocker since the rule is part of a known performance issue and any reduction is beneficial.

issues.description: No new test added to cover the fast-path skip behavior
issues.detail: The diff only adds a changeset and the regex guard. A targeted test asserting that decls with no time values are not reported (and that ones with `s`/`ms`/uppercase variants still are) would lock in the optimization against future regressions. Existing tests likely cover most cases incidentally, but a focused assertion is cheap insurance.

issues.description: Module-level regex name could be more precise
issues.detail: `HAS_TIME` reads as a definitive predicate, but the regex is really a cheap heuristic (`HAS_TIME_LIKE_TOKEN` or `MAYBE_HAS_TIME`). Renaming would make the heuristic nature explicit to future readers and reduce the chance someone removes the downstream valueParser validation thinking the regex already proved it.

dissents.topic: Whether the unitless-zero case is a real regression

positions.position: Any change in which declarations are visited by the rule body is a semantic change and must be verified by a test before merge; the regex must not narrow input scope silently.

The existing rule almost certainly only operates on word nodes with time units inside valueParser; unitless `0` was never flagged, so the regex change preserves observable behavior. The performance win is the point and merging is fine.

dissents.topic: Whether to broaden the regex to be safer

positions.position: Tighten the regex to require a word boundary or non-letter after the unit (e.g., `/\dm?s\b/i`) so identifiers like `mems` or `class1stuff` cannot pass the heuristic. Cheap to add.
False positives don't change correctness — they only fail to skip work. Adding complexity to a 1-line heuristic for a performance fix is over-engineering.

review.summary: The PR is a small, well-scoped performance fix that adds a cheap regex guard so `time-min-milliseconds` only invokes `valueParser` on declarations whose value plausibly contains a time token. The change is mostly safe: false-positive matches simply fall through to the existing logic. The one real concern is whether unitless `0` time values are still handled identically to before — the regex `/\\dm?s/i` would skip them, which is fine if the rule never flagged them (the likely case) but should be confirmed with a test. No P0 blockers; recommend a targeted test plus a minor rename of `HAS_TIME` to signal its heuristic role.
